<!-- defn-1: body_md -->
\label{defn:meandric-s}
A \textbf{meandric system} of size $n$ is a collection $\mathfrak{S}_n$ of finite, simple loops in $\mathbb{R}^2$ satisfying the following three conditions:

\begin{enumerate}
    \item No two loops in $\mathfrak{S}_n$ intersect one another.
    \item Each loop intersects the real line $\mathbb{R}$ at least twice, and no loop intersects $\mathbb{R}$ without crossing it.
    \item In total, the loops in $\mathfrak{S}_n$ cross $\mathbb{R}$ exactly $2n$ times.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end defn-1 -->
<!-- conjecture-1: body_md -->
\label{conj-a}
For every $n\geq 1$ and $x\in \mathbb{Z}+1/2$, given a box $B_n(x)$ and a uniform open meandric system, the probability that there exists both a top-left to bottom-right green crossing and a bottom-left to top-right green crossing is bounded above by $1/4$.
<!-- end conjecture-1 -->
<!-- conjecture-2: body_md -->
\label{conj-b}
Consider a box $B_n(x)$ with $x\in \mathbb{Z}+1/2$ and a uniform open meandric system. The probability that there exists both a top-left to bottom-right green crossing and a bottom-left to top-right green crossing monotonically decreases to zero as $n$ tends to infinity.
<!-- end conjecture-2 -->
<!-- conjecture-3: body_md -->
\label{conj1}
    There exists some $t=t(n)$ such that 
    \[c_n(t):=\frac{1}{2n}\mathbb{E}[S_\text{top}(2n) \cdot S^t_\text{top}(2n)]\xrightarrow[n\to \infty]{}1\]
    but
    \[p_n(t):=\mathbb{P}(A\cap A^t)\xrightarrow[n\to \infty]{}\mathbb{P}(A)\cdot\mathbb{P}(A^t)=1/4,\]
    that is, after $t=t(n)$ steps of the dynamics, the final value of the top random walk remains highly correlated with its original final value, while the box crossing events before and after the dynamics become asymptotically independent.
<!-- end conjecture-3 -->
<!-- conjecture-4: body_md -->
\label{conj2}
    There exists $\alpha,\beta>0$ with $\alpha<\beta$ such that for all $0<\varepsilon<\min\{\alpha,\beta\}$:
    \begin{itemize}
    \item If $t=t(n)=n^{\beta-\varepsilon}$, 
    \[c_n(t):=\frac{1}{2n}\mathbb{E}[S_\text{top}(2n) \cdot S^t_\text{top}(2n)]\xrightarrow[n\to \infty]{}1,\]
    but if $t=t(n)=n^{\beta+\varepsilon}$, 
    \[c_n(t):=\frac{1}{2n}\mathbb{E}[S_\text{top}(2n) \cdot S^t_\text{top}(2n)]\xrightarrow[n\to \infty]{}0.\]
    \item If $t=t(n)=n^{\alpha-\varepsilon}$,
    \[p_n(t)=\mathbb{P}(A\cap A^t)\xrightarrow[n\to \infty]{}\mathbb{P}(A)=1/2,\]
    but if $t=t(n)=n^{\alpha+\varepsilon}$,
    \[p_n(t)=\mathbb{P}(A\cap A^t)\xrightarrow[n\to \infty]{}\mathbb{P}(A)\cdot\mathbb{P}(A^t)=1/4,\]
    \end{itemize}
    that is, the decorrelation time for the ending point of the walk is of order $n^{\beta}$ but the decorrelation time for the crossing events is of order $n^{\alpha}$, that is, crossing events decorrelate much faster.
<!-- end conjecture-4 -->
